weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg3:start (f13) opens with two small grey lozenges floating in an otherwise blank upper half and a caption ('it's only 22.3') so dark it disappears; seg3:mid (f14) is a plain two-bar chart labelled 50 vs 22.3; seg3:end (f15) collapses to two hairline rules, two tiny labels and a dashed column clipped by the right frame edge, with the middle of the frame empty and a static mascot printed over 'fills a hotel'.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The title's whole premise — 216,000 tonnes melted into ONE 22.3m cube — is rendered as a length-comparison bar chart instead of the cube itself; the machine picked a generic two-bar comparison, then its end-state drops the bars entirely and leaves labels hanging in space with the value column running off-frame, while the caption layer draws low-contrast ink on the dark ground.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Draw the actual object: build a 22.3m gold cube in-frame against a to-scale Olympic pool (or a hotel lobby), sized so the cube reads as shockingly small, filling the centre of the frame; keep the comparison mark on screen through the end of the beat, pull the value column inside the safe margin, and put the caption in full-contrast ink above the ground.
